explanation.en: Ground waves travel along the earth's surface and work well at low and medium frequencies; their attenuation increases with frequency.

stem.en: Sky-wave propagation, in which waves are reflected back by the ionosphere, is used mainly in the:

explanation.en: Short-wave (HF) signals are bent back by the ionosphere, allowing long-distance communication. Higher frequencies pass through it.

stem.en: The length of a half-wave dipole for 100 MHz is:

explanation.en: λ = c/f = 3×10⁸/10⁸ = 3 m; a half-wave dipole is λ/2 = 1.5 m.

stem.en: In a Yagi–Uda TV antenna, the element that is slightly LONGER than the driven dipole and placed behind it is the:

explanation.en: The reflector (longer, behind) and directors (shorter, in front) make the antenna directional towards the station.

stem.en: An antenna that works equally well for transmitting and receiving obeys the principle of:

explanation.en: By reciprocity an antenna has the same pattern, gain and impedance whether it transmits or receives.

stem.en: Satellite TV dishes use a parabolic reflector because it:

options.en: Focuses a parallel beam onto the feed at its focus, giving very high gain

explanation.en: A paraboloid reflects waves arriving parallel to its axis to a single focus, so it is highly directional with very high gain at microwave frequencies.

stem.en: In a superheterodyne AM receiver tuned to 1000 kHz with an IF of 455 kHz, the local oscillator frequency is:

explanation.en: The local oscillator runs above the signal: fo = fs + IF = 1000 + 455 = 1455 kHz.

stem.en: The image frequency for the receiver in the previous case (fs = 1000 kHz, IF = 455 kHz) is:

explanation.en: f_image = fs + 2·IF = 1000 + 910 = 1910 kHz; it also gives a 455 kHz difference with the 1455 kHz oscillator.

stem.en: The main advantage of the superheterodyne principle is that:

options.en: Most of the gain and selectivity is at one fixed IF, so performance is uniform across the band
It removes the need for a detector

explanation.en: Every station is converted to the same IF, where fixed tuned amplifiers give high, uniform gain and selectivity.

stem.en: The purpose of AGC (automatic gain control) in a radio receiver is to:

options.en: Keep the output nearly constant for strong and weak stations

explanation.en: AGC uses the DC from the detector to reduce the gain of the RF/IF stages for strong signals, so loudness stays steady.

stem.en: The standard intermediate frequency of an FM broadcast receiver is:

explanation.en: FM broadcast receivers use a 10.7 MHz IF; AM receivers use 455 kHz.

stem.en: The stage found in an FM receiver but NOT in an AM receiver is the:

explanation.en: The limiter clips amplitude variations (noise) before the FM discriminator.

Pre-emphasis at the FM transmitter and de-emphasis at the receiver are used to:

options.en: Improve the signal-to-noise ratio at high audio frequencies

explanation.en: High audio frequencies are boosted before transmission and cut by the same amount after detection; noise picked up in between is cut too.

stem.en: In the Indian (CCIR-B/PAL) TV system, the number of lines per frame and frames per second are:

explanation.en: India uses 625 lines, 25 frames per second, shown as 50 interlaced fields per second.

stem.en: The horizontal (line) scanning frequency in the 625-line, 25-frame system is:

explanation.en: fH = 625 lines × 25 frames/s = 15 625 Hz, so each line takes 64 µs.

stem.en: In TV broadcasting, the picture and sound signals are transmitted by:

options.en: FM for picture, AM for sound
AM (vestigial sideband) for picture, FM for sound

explanation.en: The video signal uses AM with a vestigial sideband to save bandwidth; sound is FM on a carrier 5.5 MHz above the picture carrier.

stem.en: Interlaced scanning is used in television mainly to:

options.en: Reduce flicker without increasing the bandwidth

explanation.en: Odd and even lines are sent as two fields, so the screen is refreshed 50 times a second while only 25 full frames are sent.

explanation.en: λ = c/f = 3×10⁸/1.5×10⁶ = 200 m, so a quarter-wave antenna is 200/4 = 50 m long.

stem.en: The critical frequency of an ionospheric layer is 6 MHz. Using f_c = 9√N_max, its maximum electron density is about:

explanation.en: N_max = (f_c/9)² = (6×10⁶/9)² = (6.67×10⁵)² ≈ 4.4 × 10¹¹ electrons per m³.
